headline: Cell-type-resolved Mendelian randomization prioritizes disease genes across complex traits
label: Single Cell Eqtl Mendelian Randomization
summary: Single-cell eQTL data now let causal inference assign candidate disease genes to specific cell types, as in CKAP2, TRIM66, and FAM174B studies.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the move from bulk to cell-resolved genetic regulation in disease gene prioritization. Several studies pair Mendelian randomization and colocalization with single-cell eQTL or single-cell transcriptomic data to narrow candidate genes. Neuronal sc-eQTL with eQTL-pQTL MR prioritizes CKAP2 for major depressive disorder, and single-cell cis-eQTL MR with colocalization nominates astrocytic TRIM66 for trigeminal neuralgia. In COPD and lung adenocarcinoma, two-sample MR with scRNA-seq prioritizes FAM174B linked to monocyte remodeling, and AIF1 is linked to monocyte-centered networks in Alzheimer's disease. Other items map shared genetic architecture onto adrenal cell states, brain regions, and immune cell populations. The new element is cell-type specificity layered onto causal inference, with CT-FM offering a probabilistic framework to infer independent causal cell types and candidate causal variants.
